_readme: Planets, moons and the sun. These never change once the system layout is set. The sun itself is hardcoded in strategic-map.js and not listed here.

bodies.name: Hellcoast
bodies.descr:
La miniera fiammeggiante dove un’intera popolazione è dedicata all’estrazione dei rari minerali che alimentano gli armamenti dei warjammers.

### A World of Heat and Freeze

This planet is an extreme dichotomy, divided into two harshly contrasting halves. One side is eternally scorched under the blinding and relentless glare of a sun that looms unnaturally close, its surface a vast, burning desert devoured by heat. The other side is shrouded in perpetual darkness, an endless frozen tundra where the cold is so intense it bites to the bone.

For those who dare inhabit this world, survival depends on their resistance to the elements. The "Sun Side" is only habitable for creatures with a strong resistance to fire damage, while the "Space Side" is a domain reserved for those who can endure bitter cold. For all others, the conditions are lethal: they face either _extreme heat_ or _extreme cold_, with an increased Difficulty Class (DC) of 10 to survive these conditions. Creatures with some degree of resistance or tolerance to these environments begin with a DC of 5.

Society is split between these two halves. Fire Genasi, beings attuned to flames and heat, thrive on the Sun Side, while Air Genasi, whose affinity is to the cold winds, make their homes on the Space Side. Along the border that separates these two realms of extremes, several cities have emerged, dedicated to harvesting and processing rare minerals unique to each side. These cities are hubs of commerce and industry, trading goods from one extreme to the other.

An innovative solution to bridge the gap between these divided societies is the **Lightning Train**: a high-speed, electrified railway that circles the planet along the twilight line where the two worlds meet, transporting goods, people, and ideas across this stark boundary.

### The Hot Part: The Sea of Flames

On the Sun Side, the landscape is a molten hellscape—a vast sea of lava, where the ground is more liquid than solid. Gigantic ships, reinforced with heat-resistant materials, float upon this searing ocean, using the intense heat to stay aloft. These vessels are equipped with mechanisms designed to scoop minerals and rare ores directly from the molten waves. Here, everything is in constant flux, a churning cauldron of fire and rock where the air shimmers with heat and the very ground seems to breathe in waves of burning air.

Entire fleets of these ships roam the molten sea, captained by fire-resistant beings who have mastered the art of navigating this treacherous terrain. They trawl for the planet’s most precious resources—gems and metals born of fire, forged by the molten earth itself. These are then transported across the world, where they are in high demand by the denizens of the cold side.

### The Cold Part: The Frozen Expanse

On the Space Side, ships sail on seas of solid ice. These vessels glide smoothly across frozen surfaces, often equipped with skates or skis, cutting through the thick, crystalline expanse. The hulls are enchanted or constructed from materials that resist freezing and fracture, enabling them to navigate the ever-shifting landscape of icebergs and glacial cracks.

Here, minerals are not mined but extracted from towering ice formations. Massive, frozen stalagmites and caverns hold veins of rare crystals and metals trapped within, preserved for untold ages in the depths of the ice. Powerful spells or intense heat sources are used to melt the ice just enough to reach the buried treasures without shattering the fragile ecosystem that supports them.

### The Borderlands: Cities of Twilight

Between these two extremes lies a narrow band of twilight, a strip of land caught between fire and ice. This is where civilization flourishes most densely, in a precarious balance. Cities here are a blend of two worlds, where lava flows are carefully diverted into canals to heat homes, and massive ice blocks are transported in to cool the environment. Shade is key in this place: being it in the sun can immediately give 2d6 fire damage. 

Trade caravans constantly cross this border, exchanging minerals, rare herbs, and other goods unique to each side. Factories and forges use the unique resources from both realms to create tools, weapons, and artifacts of great power.

The Sunset Train is the lifeline of these border cities, ferrying goods at incredible speeds across the planet’s circumference, connecting the two extremes and maintaining a fragile balance between the realms of heat and cold.

The Sunset train lives by utilizing the blazing heat that comes from one side, using the movement generated by air.

bodies.name: Jetaras
bodies.descr:
Un deserto circonda tre ultra-città da miliardi di abitanti dominate da una gerarchia sociale immutabile.

Jetaras, the most populated planet since the fall of Meerswelt, stands as a land of stark contrasts. Its vast, sun-scorched expanse is a world where towering metropolises embody order and law, while the outlying provinces fall under the chaotic rule of ruthless Warlords.
### A Deserted Landscape

Most of Jetaras is an arid, inhospitable wasteland. Temperatures often soar to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher, creating an environment where heatstroke and dehydration are common threats to anyone who ventures too far from shelter. The land is barren, marked by endless stretches of cracked earth, desolate rock formations, and the occasional dried riverbed. The air shimmers with heat, and dust storms frequently sweep across the plains, further complicating any attempt to navigate the hostile terrain.
### The Three Great Plateaus and Ultracities

Amidst this desert lie three colossal plateaus, towering high above the scorched earth, where the climate is more temperate and suitable for human habitation. These elevated lands are home to the **Ultracities** — gargantuan urban centers where over a hundred million people live and work. These cities are marvels of human engineering, sprawling across the entire surface of the plateaus, stretching up into the skies with buildings that seem to pierce the clouds.
- **Ultracity Design:** Each Ultracity is a self-contained megastructure, organized into sectors and zones, each fulfilling a specific purpose. At the center of these cities are the "Work Towers," massive spires that serve as hubs for all forms of productivity and economic activity. These towers are multi-tiered, with factories, offices, and research labs stacked one upon another. They are the heart of the Ultracities' economic engine, humming with activity 24/7, and are the source of life for millions of workers who toil within their walls.

- **The Slums:** Surrounding the Work Towers are sprawling slums, where the majority of the population lives. These areas are dense, labyrinthine networks of makeshift buildings and cramped living spaces, where narrow alleys twist and turn in chaotic patterns. Life in the slums is tough, and survival often means navigating the complexities of a shadow economy that deals in anything from smuggled goods to black-market technology. Despite the harsh conditions, the slums are also vibrant with culture, with street markets, underground music scenes, and local traditions that create a unique sense of community.

### The Warlord Provinces

Beyond the plateaus, down in the scorched lowlands, lie the **Warlord Provinces**. Here, the grip of law and order weakens, and the land is divided among powerful warlords who rule with an iron fist. These warlords command their territories through fear and strength, maintaining private armies that patrol the borders, extort tributes, and launch raids against rivals.

- **Ravagers and Raiders:** The lowlands are also home to bands of ravagers, marauding groups who prey on the weak and isolated. They ride on the backs of **bulette**—massive, armored beasts capable of tunneling through the ground and ambushing caravans with terrifying speed and power. These raiders are experts in hit-and-run tactics, striking quickly before disappearing into the desert wastes.

- **Caravan Hunters:** Trading caravans attempting to transport goods between the Ultracities or across the provinces are at constant risk of attack. The ravagers lie in wait for these caravans, striking when they least expect it, seizing precious resources, and leaving behind only wreckage and ruin. Despite the dangers, trade remains essential, and so the caravans continue, heavily armed and always wary, with hired mercenaries and makeshift armored vehicles designed to withstand the bulettes’ assaults.
### A Land of Contrasts

Jetaras is a planet of contrasts, where order meets chaos, and civilization teeters on the edge of a vast wilderness. In the Ultracities, technology and industry reach new heights, driven by the relentless demands of survival and growth. Yet, just beyond the plateau’s edge, warlords and raiders make their own laws, thriving in a world where strength and cunning are the keys to survival. It is a world constantly on the brink, where every journey is fraught with danger, every choice has its consequences, and the future is as unforgiving as the desert sun.

bodies.name: The void
bodies.descr:
Ciò che rimane di ciò che una volta era. Il vuoto è ora una fonte costante di invasioni demoniache e spetta ai custodi assicurarsi che non sfuggano nello spazio più ampio. I custodi vivono nella piccola città-roccia di Bral.

The Void is all that remains of the once-thriving planet of Meerswelt. Now, it is a desolate expanse—a shattered graveyard of floating debris, where countless asteroids drift through the cold, empty darkness. These fragments are the remnants of the old world, broken pieces of land from the destroyed planet, scattered across the cosmos like the shards of a forgotten dream.

At the center of this vast, ruined sea, a greenish vapor swirls, growing denser and darker the closer one gets to the middle. This fog is thick with an otherworldly malevolence, a choking miasma that wraps around everything it touches. At its heart lies a small, insatiable black hole, pulling all matter toward it—a one-way ticket to the Abyss, a gateway to a dimension of destruction and death.

But even here, amidst the ruins, there are those who survive. On some of the larger asteroids, pockets of determined warriors and exiles make their stand. They eke out a living among the rocks, fighting back the endless waves of demons and horrors that emerge from the depths of the Abyss, battling for survival against the very embodiment of chaos and annihilation.

#### La città dei mille popoli

La Roccia di Bral, anche chiamata soltanto Bral, è la città spaziale più ricca e variegata fra tutte quelle esistenti. Fondata da una ciurma di Hadozee, è diventata nel corso del tempo un polo interculturale secondo a nessuno. Ogni giorno migliaia di oggetti, spezie, magie vengono venduti all'interno del suo mercato centrale, mentre creature di dimensioni diverse conversano all'interno delle sue taverne. Bral orbita Tel-Ul-Kal, il pianeta d'origine dei Thri-Kreen, ed è un satellite di Luce, un insieme di gas bluastri che si concentrano al centro del Primospazio creando la luce che illumina l'intero opazio. Bral non è una città governabile: ogni quartiere, ogni strada, e addiritturaogni edificio ha il suo set di tradizioni, regole e punizioni. Pertanto la corona di Starhaven, in questo momento portata dal Principe Jacques Marat, è sempre stata attenta (salvo rari casi) ad approcciare il governo della città con un elevato distaccamento, intervenendo soltanto quando la sicurezza dell'asteroide stesso veniva minacciata. Di conseguenza, Bral è una città senza legge: i suoi abitanti e turisti devono proteggersi da soli, anche se la città non è impassibile al crimine e spesso soccorre i più bisognosi. L'asteroide si organizza in cinque grandi sezioni.

#### High City

La città alta è dove risiede Starhaven, la reggia del principe Jacques, e le ville dell'Alta nobiltà di Bral. Probabilmente una delle aree più ricche dell'intero spazio conosciuto, è pattugliata e controllata dalla Guardia Regale. Qui la legge del Prinicipe è assoluta, e il crimine non è tollerato: gli audaci che provano a oltrepassare senza permesso le mura che dividono l'Alta Città dal resto di Bral si ritrovano velocemente imprigionati nelle Segrete, con molti di loro che non rivedono poi mai più la luce delle stelle. Costanti festini sono organizzati dalla coorte per l'Alta Città, e l'intera area è uno dei punti di maggiore scambio culturale dello spazio conosciuto, con artisti e scienziati che costantemente vengono invitati dietro le mura di Starhaven. Qui è dove anche si incontra, quando chiamato, il Gran Concilio delle comunità Hadozee, e sono considerati parte dell'alta città anche il Distretto dei Templi e lo spazio che arriva fino al Piazzale Estivo.

#### Middle City

La città di mezzo è dove risiede il cuore mercantile di Bral: la stragrande maggioranza delle attività commerciali, gilde e organizzazioni ha sede in questa sezione. La maggior parte delgi edifici di quest'area è composta da diversi piani, dove solitamente i primi due sono dediti ad attività commerciali mentre quelli superiori fungono da abitazioni per il ceto medio di Bral. La sicurezza della città di mezzo è affidata a una apposita Gilda, finanziata dalle altre gilde commerciali: qui il più grande crimine è il furto, che viene poco tollerato, mentre crimini di altra specie sono invece solitamente lasciati alle comunità che risiedono all'interno dei diversi quartieri. Una tassa viene pagata a Starhaven per la protezione militare che viene fornita e il cibo che viene razionato nella città, ma per il resto la gestione politica dell'area è in mano alle Gilde che si sono organizzate in un "Cartello Politico", di fatto l'organo di governo in faccende non militari o estere. La burocrazia è molto diffusa all'interno di quest'area, ed è molto difficile che non-Braliani (i non nati a Bral) possano aver accesso alle case e appartamenti della città di Mezzo

#### Low City

È dove la classe di lavoratori e immigrati risiede a Bral: è un'area dura e severa, anche se non senza legge. Qui il crimine è comune, le strade sono sporche e caotiche, e le case si stagliano per divesi piani gli uni ammassati sopra gli altri. Ciononostante forti gruppi locali, chiamati Clan, controllano piccole aree della città (anche solo dei singoli palazzi) garantendo protezione e sicurezza ai loro membri, e scontrandosi con altri per proteggere le proprie risorse: è raro però che in questi costanti scontri scappi il morto, in quanto generalemente la violenza che domina le strade non è così severa. L'area è di fatto controllato da una serie di potenti organizzazioni criminali, che però fanno attenzione a non inimincarsi Starhaven. Nonostante questi aspetti negativi, la Low City si rivela anche essere il cuore pulsante di Bral: è qui che vive e sprizza la fame di successo che definisce l'identità braliana, mostrandosi in un array di infinite varietà di persone, interessi e cultire che si scontrano in un unico minestrone.

#### Il Dungeon

È il sistema di fogne, caverne e tunnel che formano l'interno dell'astroide di Bral. Nessuno ha mai mappato in completezza questa rete di tunnel, in quanto sembra sempre espandersi e cambiare, così tanto che molti sono convinti che il posto sia pulsante di energia arcana. Qui è dove si organizzano i criminali, si muovono le merci contraffatte, e si nascondono figure oscure che tramano nell'ombra. La parte dei tunnel frontale, sotto il bordo estremo della lowcity, mostra una enorme caverna aperta allo spazio che viene usata come hangar per le navi che arivano sull'asteroide.

#### Il Sottosopra

L'altro lato dell'asteroide è dove risiedono i campi di cibo che vengono usati per sfamare la città dall'altra parte e la cittadella centrale dell'Esercito di Bral. L'accesso a quest'area è vietato alla stragrande maggioranza della popolazione, e i campi vengono lavorati da prigionieri e schiavi controllati dall'esercito. Qui è anche dove si trovano le vele, gigantesci appartati che vengono usati per girare l'asteroide e gestire le luce che esso riceve.

bodies.name: Draconia
bodies.descr:
Draghi e avidità governano questa terra ma i veri re di questo pianeta sono i possenti eserciti dei Wueng che piegano tutti al loro volere.

A Planet of Fire and Storms, Quakes, and Tsunamis: A World Ruled by Chromatic Dragons in an Endless War for Gold. Amidst the chaos, adventurers and opportunists seek their share.
## A Warped Planet

Once, Draconia was a barren world, covered in vast stretches of blue and red prairies that painted the surface in vibrant colors. However, since the arrival of the dragons, the planet has begun to deform under the magical influence of these legendary creatures, transforming in irreversible ways over nearly 200 years of colonization. Now, each Lord of the Land molds the world around them, and all other creatures can do nothing but adapt:
- **Masters of Fire (Ancient Red Dragons):** They shape the mountains they inhabit into volcanoes and seas of magma. Their territories are dominated by fire and flames, where rivers of molten rock flow, and the air itself sizzles with heat.
- **Masters of the Earth (Ancient Black Dragons):** These dragons rule from deep chasms and gorges, cracks in the earth that descend into the very depths of the world. At the bottom of these places, sulfuric acid lakes bubble and steam, serving as resting places for the Masters of the Earth.
- **Masters of Ice (Ancient White Dragons):** They transform their surroundings into icy tundras, inhospitable and frozen wastelands where temperatures easily drop 40 degrees below zero. Often residing near the poles, their lands rarely see sunlight, often covered by thick layers of clouds that obscure the sky.
- **Masters of the Waves (Ancient Blue Dragons):** Dwelling among small, scattered islands in the sea, they thrive amidst perpetual storms. The entire sea of Draconia is electrified, with constant and erratic discharges of electricity that ripple across the world, turning the waters into a treacherous expanse.
- **Masters of Nature (Ancient Green Dragons):** These dragons reign over vast stretches of lush vegetation, where monstrous creatures slither through the leaves, ready to devour anyone who dares venture into these territories. Their domains are dense, vibrant jungles that pulse with life and danger.

These domains often stretch for miles upon miles, creating isolated islands of deformity in an otherwise barren world.
## A World of Monsters

Dragons are the undisputed rulers of these lands, controlling the very life force of Draconia. As creatures of immense ego and strength, they frequently clash with each other, igniting wars to consume one another's resources. Younger dragons often lead assaults against their sires to usurp their place, making peace nothing more than a fleeting fantasy. Yet, despite this brutal reality, Draconia is also inhabited by millions of humanoids who, one way or another, serve their draconic overlords. The Cult of Tiamat is the dominant faith across the planet, and all its inhabitants see the dragons more as celestial beings than demons; loyalty to a Master is generously rewarded, and entire cities and kingdoms dedicate themselves in exchange for protection.
The majority of the population is concentrated in the domains of the Masters of Nature, who are the most amiable and socially adept of all the chromatic dragons. Draconian society largely thrives among them, but significant numbers also serve the other dragons in various forms of servitude, from menial laborers to devoted cultists.
## The Chosen of the Queen

Amidst this chaos, one faction is undeniably dominant over all others: the Wueng family. Descendants of Zai Wueng, the Voice of Tiamat, they enjoy the blessing of the Dragon Queen herself and wield the power to bend all the dragons of this world to their will. Their rule is one of necessity, allowing their subjects free reign but intervening with an iron fist only when needed. The Wuengs are as wealthy as the oldest dragons and can summon these hordes of dragons to their service at will. For this reason, they possess no standing army or fleet, instead using a chromatic horde whenever they need to punish other families.
## The Metallic Cloaks

Moving stealthily between domains, hunted by almost every inhabitant of Draconia, are the dragons and humanoid followers of Bahamut. Protected by their ability to polymorph into humanoid forms, gold, bronze, and other metallic dragons oppose and sabotage their distant chromatic cousins, sometimes even managing to kill them in surprise attacks. 

These "Metallic Cloaks" live in the shadows, relying on subterfuge, guerrilla tactics, and their unique abilities to survive. They whisper of a future where Draconia is free of the chromatic dominion, seeking allies among the oppressed and those who dare dream of rebellion.

bodies.name: Tithion
bodies.descr:
Casa delle orde di orchi che così spesso discendono nel sistema sotto il comando dei loro leader per soddisfare la loro sete di sangue uccidendo e sottomettendo pianeti ribelli.

Thithoin is a wet moon, its surface almost entirely submerged beneath a vast sea of rare, dark-purple acid. This corrosive ocean stretches as far as the eye can see, broken only by the jagged peaks of a few lonely mountains that rise like islands from the bubbling expanse. The acid is volatile, hissing and steaming when it contacts anything not adapted to its potent nature, and it is so caustic that it melts most materials, making transport and construction nearly impossible.

Yet, from this dangerous sea, tall plants have evolved to thrive. Their thick trunks rise high above the surface, covered in bark that is impervious to the acid’s bite. These trees, known as Vardenwood, draw nutrients from what the acid dissolves, their roots submerged deep in the purple depths. Their dense, fibrous wood is one of the few substances that can endure the acid’s corrosive nature, making it invaluable for constructing rafts, dwellings, and containers to navigate and live on this great, churning swamp.

The air on Thithoin is filled with a sharp, acrid scent, and a faint violet mist often lingers over the surface of the acid sea, casting an eerie glow over the twisted silhouettes of the Vardenwood groves.

bodies.name: Enov
bodies.descr:
Qualcosa di più simile a una fortezza che a un pianeta in cui si nascondono ricchezze oltre ogni immaginazione. Il pianeta è la riserva di tutte le risorse del sistema.

Enov is a warm, green moon, its surface covered mostly by rolling fields of short, emerald grass that sway gently in the constant breeze. The landscape is dotted with rivers and lakes, their waters shimmering under the bright sun, but none of them find their way to an ocean. Instead, they flow into the deep cracks that fracture the ground, vast chasms that split the earth like ancient scars.

As the water tumbles into these endless abysses, it evaporates into fine mist, vanishing into the depths before reaching any visible bottom. The vapor rises back up, forming thick, drifting clouds that swirl across the sky, creating a perpetual cycle of water and air. The clouds cast soft shadows over the grassy plains, while the cracks below seem to whisper with a quiet, mysterious energy, hinting at secrets buried deep within the heart of the planet.

bodies.name: Ion
bodies.descr:
Montagne aride e fredde circondano il Faro della Conoscenza l’unica università di magia del sistema. Qui vengono formati alcuni dei più grandi maghi dei nostri tempi.

## Quick Look

Ion is a stark and desolate world, characterized by its barren, grey landscapes and a striking lack of life. The planet is dominated by a single prominent city, the Beacon, which gleams with countless small blue lights. This university of unparalleled renown is shielded by a thin layer of magically maintained breathable air. Outside this protective dome, the atmosphere is non-existent, rendering the rest of the planet uninhabitable.
##### The Flow of Knowledge
On Ion, the environment fosters unparalleled intellectual growth. Any creature on this planet benefits from a +2 bonus to their Intelligence score, with the maximum score increased by the same amount. Additionally, beings on Ion have advantage on rolls when attempting to recall information in the fields of Arcana, History, Nature, and Religion. This enhancement makes Ion an extraordinary center for knowledge and scholarly pursuits, where intellectual capabilities are significantly amplified.

## An Undead Planet

The history of Ion is enveloped in mystery. It seems to have appeared in the system only recently, as historical records from two thousand years ago make no mention of it. The planet remains cloaked in darkness, with the sun merely a distant point in the ever-black sky. Its surface is largely barren, with a few densely populated cities dependent on food imports from the surrounding moons.

The majority of Ion's inhabitants are arcane and scientific researchers affiliated with a prestigious academy known as "the Beacon," which is controlled by the influential Ntsu family. [[Beacon]] is the sole known stronghold of Vecna's cult, where his teachings are both practiced and revered. Here, mages are renowned throughout the system for their formidable power and deep arcane knowledge. Ion is a magnet for those seeking to elevate their understanding to unparalleled levels, attracting researchers who require that extra spark of inspiration.

## A Planet of Secrets

Ion stands as a sanctuary for knowledge and secrets. Every researcher who arrives on the planet must relinquish all personal knowledge and allow their entire existence to be cataloged and stored in the vast, enigmatic archives of the Beacon. Powerful magic is intricately woven into both the people and the records of the Beacon, with information tightly guarded and restricted from casual access. Inhabitants of Ion live in accordance with Vecna's demands for secrecy and silence, embracing the weight of the hidden knowledge they possess.

## The Terror

In addition to its barren lands, harsh climate, and inhospitable environment, Ion is notorious for one final, terrifying aspect: the Terror. This curse is unlike any other, capable of reducing even the mightiest of warriors to a state of perpetual child-like fear. Those afflicted by the Terror experience profound dread and anxiety that persists until they leave the planet, often leaving them traumatized. The origins and selection criteria of the Terror remain unknown, and there is no known cure. The only escape for those struck by this curse is to depart Ion permanently.

*From nothing, I suddenly felt everything, thousand souls, things, animals demons and all what life has ever shown me and then more. Then they turned, evil no human can hold washing over me, taking me, burning me, torturing me. All was black, no life, no thought. I cried, I screamed, I was nowhere and everywhere. One thing was clear, death was the only hope. I was no more in spirit, I hoped for my body to follow. Never I will touch that cursed land, ever again.*

bodies.name: Tophadus
bodies.descr:
L’acqua è il luogo da cui provengono le navi. Una luna oceanica dove i Carxus hanno costruito per la prima volta i loro grandi warjammers navi che ora dominano il sistema.

Tophadus is an ocean world, where life clings to the few shallow banks that rise from its endless, deep waters. These banks, where the ocean is less deep, are the heart of society, dotted with structures that rise like spires above the waves or plunge deep into the watery abyss. Buildings are designed to withstand not just the constant moisture but the ferocity of the sea itself—reinforced to endure the sudden hurricanes that sweep across the planet, their waves towering up to a hundred meters high.

Life on Tophadus is layered and vertical. The uppermost levels of society live close to the surface, in gleaming towers that pierce the skies, always watching the horizon for the next great storm. Below them, cities extend deep into the ocean, a maze of glass domes, pressurized chambers, and submersible tunnels. The deeper one descends, the harsher and darker the environment becomes. Here, in the lowest reaches, spelljammers—experimental vessels designed to withstand extreme conditions—are tested in crushing depths, where the water pressure can crumple steel like paper.

Every layer of Tophadus society has adapted to the ocean's unpredictable wrath, from the high towers to the depths below, all moving in a delicate dance with the planet’s volatile nature.

bodies.name: Hoter
bodies.descr:
Una luna di gas governata da navi che fluttuano sulla sua superficie filtrando e raccogliendo un potente afrodisiaco usato dagli stozav per creare le loro sostanze potenziate.

Hoter is a gas moon, a swirling world with no solid ground to anchor its inhabitants. Instead, cities are built on massive floating platforms, drifting across a vast, ever-changing sea of clouds. The platforms ride the powerful winds that surge through the dense layers of toxic gases beneath them, their stability a constant balance between engineering and the unpredictable currents below.

The atmosphere of Hoter is a dangerous mix: some of the gases are acidic and deadly, capable of dissolving metal and flesh alike, while others are potent hallucinogens, sought after by those brave or foolish enough to harvest them. These rare gases are distilled to create Hosshine, a powerful drug that is coveted across the system for its mind-altering properties.

Deep within the gaseous layers, strange creatures are said to dwell, unseen and mysterious. Few have glimpsed them, but their presence is felt—a low, distant rumble in the winds or a sudden, chilling shadow that passes beneath the platforms. Most inhabitants fear these beings, for when they do rise from the depths, they bring tales of horror and madness in their wake.

bodies.name: Zimurn
bodies.descr:
Isole fluttuanti ospitano una legge radicata. Una società in cui la legge è tutto e la deviazione è il più grande crimine.

Zimurn is a moon of barren expanses, where the ground itself seems to defy gravity. Floating islands and drifting asteroids hover in the thin atmosphere, casting long, ethereal shadows across the rocky surface below. These islands, suspended in a delicate dance, are often cloaked in mist and connected by fragile bridges of rope, vine, or weathered stone.

Life here is sparse but resilient, with fungi and plants that thrive in the dim light. These bioluminescent species cling to the jagged rocks, glowing faintly in shades of blue, green, and violet, painting the landscape in a soft, otherworldly light. Their spores drift lazily through the air, carried by the ever-present wind that whispers between the islands.

On these floating isles stand the ancient Temples of Justice, carved from the stone itself and adorned with thick carpets of moss and glowing lichen. The temples are places of solemnity and reflection, where the few who call Zimurn home come to seek guidance or pass judgment. The isolation of the islands, suspended between the sky and the emptiness of space, lends an air of mystery and reverence to these sanctuaries, making them a beacon for those seeking truth in the shadows of a lonely moon.

bodies.name: Saltar
bodies.descr:
Un pianeta che può essere attraversato a piedi dove le città si espandono in profondità piuttosto che in larghezza. Letale se lasciata incontrollata qui gli Ousssek tramano i loro grandi piani di dominio.

**Saltar** is a unique and enigmatic world, resembling a massive piece of pumice stone floating in the void of space. From a distance, its surface appears rough and riddled with countless holes, like a vast, porous sponge suspended against the backdrop of the cosmos. The planet has no atmosphere, leaving its inhabitants to gaze directly upon the stars that blaze across the sky in unfiltered clarity. Ruled by the [[Ousssek]].

### A Hollow World of Caverns and Darkness

The surface of Saltar is riddled with countless pores, craters, and crevices that open into vast underground expanses. These caverns and tunnels twist and turn in a chaotic labyrinth, plunging deep into the planet’s crust. Here, **civilizations of drow** (dark elves) have evolved, adapting to their unique environment in a manner reminiscent of the Underdark—the deep and dangerous subterranean realm known on other worlds.

- **Surface and the Pores:** The surface is almost completely barren, with no atmosphere to sustain life. The terrain is jagged and rugged, with craters that pockmark the landscape like the surface of a pumice stone. The pores vary in size, some as small as a cave entrance and others large enough to swallow entire cities. These openings lead down into a network of sprawling underground caverns.

- **Underground Civilizations:** Within these expansive caverns, the drow have built their societies. Cut off from the sun and exposed to the chill of the void, they have developed unique ways to survive. Cities cling to the walls of these vast cavities, with bridges and tunnels connecting outposts across great distances. Bioluminescent fungi and glowing crystals provide the only sources of light, creating an eerie yet beautiful luminescence that dances on the cavern walls. The deeper one ventures, the less light there is, until only the most hardened creatures dare to explore the depths.

### The Blue Sea: A Watery Sphere of Power

At the very core of Saltar lies the planet’s most mysterious feature: **The Blue Sea**—a massive, suspended sphere of water, almost two miles in diameter, that glows with an ethereal greenish-blue light. It appears as if it defies gravity, floating weightlessly at the center of the hollow planet, casting a strange luminescence through the surrounding rock.

- **A Storm in the Core:** The Blue Sea is a source of unimaginable power. Within this watery sphere, great bolts of lightning constantly form and flash, shooting outward through the entire structure of the planet. These electrical discharges propagate through the porous rock, creating a network of crackling energy that can be seen and heard throughout the depths of Saltar. The drow revere the Blue Sea as a source of both life and destruction, as the lightning bolts occasionally find their way through caverns, striking with deadly force and igniting underground storms.

- **The Elemental Nature:** Scholars and mages speculate that the Blue Sea is some sort of elemental font or a tear in reality where the elemental planes intersect. The water itself is highly unusual; it is both liquid and plasma, a mysterious substance that defies normal properties. The drow have learned to harness the energy of the Blue Sea for their own purposes—using its power to fuel arcane rituals, light their cities, and defend against external threats.

### A Planet Without an Atmosphere

Saltar has no atmosphere, and its surface is exposed directly to the cold vacuum of space. As a result, its surface is a dead, airless expanse where no life can survive unaided. However, the lack of atmosphere also means that those who stand near the entrances to the deeper caverns can see the stars in unparalleled clarity, unobstructed by any atmospheric distortion. This sight has given rise to a unique culture of **stargazers and astronomers** among the drow, who study the stars from these exposed positions, seeking meaning and guidance in the cosmic patterns.

### A Planet of Secrets and Mysteries

Saltar is a world full of contradictions—a dead world with a vibrant, thriving underworld; a place of perpetual darkness, yet illuminated by the strange glow of the Blue Sea; a realm where civilizations endure in the depths, all the while surrounded by the cold, harsh void of space. It is a place where mysteries abound, from the true nature of the Blue Sea to the origins of the planet's strange, porous structure.

bodies.name: Calichi
bodies.descr:
Nulla è stabile qui tranne la distruzione costante. Costantemente colpita da disastri naturali questa società vive per sopravvivere un altro giorno.

Calichi is a moon of relentless tectonic activity, where the surface is a chaotic realm of molten lava and floating landmasses. These continents, vast and drifting, bob and weave on the seething sea of magma below, their edges often glowing with the intense heat of the lava they skim. The lava sea roils and churns, its fiery tendrils reaching up toward the floating lands that drift above.

The continents on Calichi are large enough to support life, but their stability is far from guaranteed. The moon’s constant seismic activity means that collisions between these drifting masses are frequent. When continents collide, the resulting earthquakes are catastrophic, sending shockwaves through the land and causing massive volcanic eruptions that reshape the landscape in an instant.

Additionally, the dynamic interaction between lava and land leads to other natural disasters. When a sea of molten rock crashes into a continent, it triggers enormous hurricanes that whip across the surface, fueled by the intense heat and steam. These storms can ravage the land, stripping away vegetation and reshaping the terrain with their ferocious winds.

Despite the dangers, life on Calichi has adapted to the harsh conditions. The inhabitants live in fortified structures built to withstand the constant tremors and eruptions, and they have developed sophisticated techniques to predict and survive the frequent disasters. Their cities are perched on the edges of continents, anchored with advanced technologies that keep them stable amid the ever-shifting land. The breathtaking and tumultuous beauty of Calichi is matched only by its peril, creating a world where resilience and adaptability are the keys to survival.

bodies.name: Allenia
bodies.descr:
Il ghiaccio e il gelo non hanno fermato la natura su questa luna. Un mondo-prigione qui vengono mandati tutti gli indesiderabili a vivere in una brutale società di tribù goblinoidi in guerra per gli scarti che i loro padroni lasciano.

This moon is a rugged, mountainous world, perpetually blanketed in cold. Its surface is dominated by dense, dark pink forests, where towering trees with jet-black bark stretch skyward, absorbing every precious ray of light that filters through the gloom. These trees are adapted to the moon’s harsh conditions, their dark color a necessity for capturing the scarce light that penetrates the heavy, overcast skies.

The peaks of the mountains are capped with a striking feature—mirror-like musk that reflects away the light. This reflective substance shimmers like liquid mercury, creating dazzling patterns and illusions as it casts sunlight back into the sky. The contrast between the absorbing darkness of the forests and the blinding brightness of the reflective peaks results in a landscape that is both mesmerizing and disorienting. The interplay of light and shadow makes navigation treacherous, as familiar landmarks shift and distort, while the shifting reflections off the musk create a surreal, almost hallucinatory environment.

In this confusing terrain, the dense forests are alive with the eerie whispers of the wind through the blackened trees, and the reflective peaks cast shifting, ghostly patterns across the landscape. The moon’s landscape is a place where survival depends on mastering the deceptive play of light and shadow, and where the natural beauty is intertwined with the constant challenge of navigating a bewildering world.

bodies.name: Aepra
bodies.descr:
Una luna governata fino a poco tempo fa da una guerra civile costante; ora una nuova famiglia cerca di destreggiarsi tra odi secolari e l’influenza dei potenti e vicini Ousssek.

Aepra is a wandering moon, caught in the gravitational pull of three different planets, its orbit an unpredictable dance through space. This erratic path throws Aepra from one extreme to another, its surface scorched by blistering heat one moment, then plunged into frigid darkness the next. The temperatures swing wildly between searing and freezing, rendering the surface inhospitable to life.

To survive, the inhabitants have retreated underground, building a hidden society in vast networks of tunnels and caverns carved out by enormous creatures known as the humber hulks. These colossal beasts burrow through the rock, their massive maws grinding through the earth and leaving behind vast, labyrinthine passageways. Within these winding depths, life on Aepra thrives, shielded from the deadly temperature shifts above.

The underground cities are illuminated by glowing fungi and bioluminescent crystals embedded in the cave walls, casting a dim, otherworldly light. The architecture is shaped around the natural curves and tunnels left by the humber hulks, creating a living labyrinth where communities grow and adapt to the ever-changing environment of their moon. Here, in the belly of the earth, societies have evolved in tune with the rhythms of their strange, subterranean world, always mindful of the creatures that both provide their shelter and could one day turn their world to rubble.

bodies.name: Wandacker
bodies.descr:
Una delle famiglie più potenti non vivono sul pianeta stesso infestato da gnoll. Invece appaltano navi equipaggiamenti e altre risorse a contractor suicidi che cercano costantemente di fare il colpo grosso e raccogliere qualcosa di prezioso dalla superficie di Wandacker.

AWandacker is a picturesque world of warmth and fertility, seemingly ideal for civilization. However, it is marred by constant gnoll invasions, making survival outside of fortified military bases exceedingly difficult.
### The Blood Plains

Wandacker’s terrain is characterized by its jagged, rocky formations, red-hued steppes, and seas of black mercury. The northern hemisphere is predominantly land, where vast expanses of rugged landscape and rich resources dominate. Among these resources is **Borzatium**, one of the most potent minerals in the system.

The planet enjoys mostly sunny weather, but it is occasionally besieged by "Maelstorms"—violent and toxic tornadoes of mercury that emanate from the seas. These storms are both destructive and hazardous, spreading corrosive mercury across the landscape.

### Borzatium

**Borzatium** is a mineral with remarkable properties. It can be shaped and modified through the cantrip _Mold Earth_, retaining the fundamental characteristics of iron but with the added versatility of magical manipulation. This unique quality makes Borzatium a highly coveted resource for crafting and construction, despite the dangers associated with its extraction.

### An Uninhabitable Planet

While Wandacker's natural beauty and resource abundance make it a world of potential, the reality is far from ideal. The surface is overrun by hordes of gnolls—vicious and destructive creatures that relentlessly attack any form of civilization. These marauding gnolls wreak havoc across the plains, rendering the planet’s fertile lands perilous and largely uninhabitable.

Civilization has been pushed to the higher elevations, taking refuge in the peaks of scattered mountains. These elevated fortresses serve as bastions of safety against the gnoll menace. The mountains themselves are rich in valuable resources, including Borzatium, precious food sources, and other essential materials, but accessing these resources requires navigating through dangerous gnoll-infested areas.

### The Struggle for Survival

The gnoll invasion has created a desperate struggle for survival. Military bases and fortified cities are strategically placed in the mountainous regions, where they can defend against the gnolls' attacks while exploiting the land's resources. The conflict between the gnolls and the inhabitants of Wandacker has led to a constant state of tension and skirmishes, with frequent expeditions launched to secure valuable resources and protect the fragile remnants of civilization.

In summary, Wandacker is a world of stark contrasts—its inherent beauty and resource wealth are overshadowed by the gnoll threat. While its sunny climate and rich mineral deposits present opportunities, the pervasive danger and the need for constant vigilance and defense shape the daily lives of its inhabitants.

bodies.name: Tebara
bodies.descr:
Una società aristocratica schiavista che coltiva la maggior parte del cibo per il sistema.

Tebara is a moon of remarkable beauty and serenity, a lush, idyllic world that seems to embody the very essence of perpetual spring and summer. Its vast, rolling fields are a patchwork of vibrant greens and golden hues, rich with abundant flora and flourishing with life. The climate here is consistently mild and pleasant, characterized by gentle breezes and clear skies that make each day feel like a continuation of the best season of the year.

The landscape is dotted with shimmering lakes and meandering rivers, their waters crystal-clear and teeming with life. Verdant meadows stretch endlessly, framed by picturesque hills and valleys, creating a scene of pastoral perfection that seems untouched by time. The weather is consistently favorable, with warm, sunlit days and cool, refreshing evenings that invite outdoor living and celebration.

Near the equator, the land changes abruptly into arid desert, a stark contrast to the lushness of the temperate regions. However, this desert region is mostly hidden beneath the vast expanse of equatorial seas that cover it, leaving the arid landscape largely unseen and unexplored. The seas themselves are expansive and tranquil, their serene waters reflecting the clear blue skies and adding to the moon's overall charm.

Inhabitants of Tebara enjoy a life of ease and abundance, surrounded by natural beauty and favorable conditions. The moon’s rich environment and stable weather make it a paradise, where each day is a celebration of the idyllic harmony between land and sky.

bodies.name: Hophus
bodies.descr:
Oscurità e dolore sono sovrani su questa luna senza sole.

KMoon of [[Wandacker]].

Hophus is a moon shrouded in perpetual darkness, locked in a synchronous orbit with its home planet, Wandacker. This unique positioning ensures that Hophus is always hidden from the light of its distant sun, entirely obscured by the looming bulk of Wandacker. As a result, the moon's surface is enshrouded in an eternal twilight, illuminated only by the faint, distant glow of Wandacker's reflection against the dark expanse of space.

The terrain of Hophus is a stark and rugged landscape, characterized by jagged, craggy rocks and a myriad of craters. These craters, some of immense size, are filled with ancient, frozen water, their icy contents shimmering with a cold, ghostly luminescence in the moon’s perpetual gloom. The ice appears almost like crystal, reflecting the scarce light that manages to filter through the gloom, creating an eerie, otherworldly glow within the craters.

The constant darkness and extreme cold have rendered Hophus a desolate, isolated world. The absence of sunlight and the harsh environment make it an inhospitable place for most forms of life, leaving the moon's surface a silent testament to the vast, unfeeling cosmos.

bodies.name: Enides
bodies.descr:
Un centro di ricerca e creazione gli Shawel sono una famiglia che ha sempre eccelso nella creazione di manufatti magici.

This small moon, barely more than an asteroid, drifts quietly through space, its surface barren and unremarkable. The landscape is a desolate expanse of rocky debris and dust, with no significant features to break the monotony of its grey, pitted terrain.

The moon's only notable characteristic is a curious formation: a large, translucent white opaz, a crystalline structure that seems to contain a liquid. This opaz shimmers faintly in the light, its surface rippling with an ethereal glow that hints at the mysterious fluid trapped within. The liquid inside the opaz moves slowly, like a viscous, luminescent jelly, occasionally catching the light and casting a soft, shimmering reflection across the surrounding rocks.

Despite its intriguing appearance, the opaz remains largely ignored. The liquid within it has proven to be of little practical use, its properties enigmatic and its applications unknown. Researchers and explorers who visit the moon often speculate about its origin and purpose, but no significant advancements or discoveries have emerged from studying it. As a result, the moon remains a silent, enigmatic body in space, its sole claim to fame the enigmatic opaz that offers no answers, only questions.

bodies.name: El-Beth-El
bodies.descr:
Quattro regni su un pianeta con un unico padrone su tutti. La Mano è un nuovo arrivato nel sistema e deve rapidamente bilanciare tutti i problemi brucianti e distruttivi lasciati dai loro predecessori.

Il pianeta si chiama El-beth-el. Un piccolo pianeta “tidally-locked” il cui asse di rotazione è ortogonale al sole provocando condizioni climatiche tanto uniche quanto difficili. 
#### Nareb, la Luce
La parte del pianeta rivolta verso il sole è chiamata Nareb, che significa "Terra bruciata". Quelle terre calde sono per la maggior parte deserti di sabbia e polvere, spezzati da catene montuose ricche di minerali. Le zone vicine al polo, comunemente chiamato l'Occhio, sono inabitabili a causa delle temperature estreme. Le storie raccontano di deserti vetrificati, alberi di pietra e piogge di ossidiana. Questa ossidiana prende il nome di **Specchio dell’Abisso**. La lama di [[Arren Akbe]] ne é composta.
#### Eubdesh, l’Ombra
La parte oscura invece è chiamata Eubdesh, "guidata dalle stelle". Deserti gelati, antiche città in rovina e coste sferzate da venti gelidi. Tutto illuminato solo dalla tenue luce delle stelle e delle tre lune. Le creature della notte che abitano quei luoghi alimentano le leggende di tutto il pianeta e solo poche tribù e popoli nomadi vi abitano.
#### Lerei, il Crepuscolo
Infine, le regioni intorno all'equatore sono chiamate Lerei, le terre dell'alba eterna. La maggior parte della vita e degli insediamenti umani si trovano in quei luoghi, gli unici in cui si possono trovare fiumi, mari e temperature abbastanza miti da coltivare.
#### Khor Galimah, la Capitale
La capitale del pianeta, dove risiede la famiglia imperiale, si chiama Khor Galimah. E' una realtà totalmente a parte. Lì abitano persone di ogni razza e provenienza, viaggiatori, mercanti, nobili e in generale individui a contatto con la cultura interplanetaria del sistema.

Ciò che si può vedere a Khor Galimah è in forte contrasto con il resto del pianeta, dove si trovano numerose culture totalmente isolate dalla realtà della capitale e del resto del sistema.
# I popoli e le nazioni di El-beth-el

Su El-beth-el ci sono quattro principali nazioni organizzate che si estendono più o meno a cavallo di [Lerei](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.lafidefp8m9x). Le loro culture sono simili ma profondamente plasmate dalle condizioni climatiche estreme.
## Kerr
Kerr è la nazione più grande e potente, governata dalla monarchia eterna del [Re Fanciullo Akmaral II](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.o5s8rj8heu62) . Si trova fra [Lerei](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.lafidefp8m9x) e [Nareb](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.xft0p67hdcy0) ed è di stampo estetico arabo-turco: palazzi adornati con cupole scintillanti, bazar profumati di spezie e vesti dai ricami d'oro. La società è rigidamente stratificata, e la monarchia eterna è venerata come divina. Kerr domina il commercio di minerali rari estratti dalle sue montagne, ma le sue terre esterne, bruciate dal sole, sono popolate da clan nomadi e predoni che sfidano l'autorità centrale.
### Akmaral II, il Re Fanciullo
A Kerr c'è una monarchia assoluta guidata dal Re Fanciullo Akmaral II, che decenni fa fu maledetto a rimanere per sempre bambino. La maledizione fa anche sì che il re sia spesso soggetto a criptiche e grandiose visioni del futuro. Ad affiancarlo e consigliarlo, c'è la *Cabala*: una cerchia ristretta di nobili, ricchi mercanti, religiosi e rappresentanti del popolo il cui scopo principale è proteggere il Re e interpretare le sue visioni. Il governo vero e proprio di Kerr è in mano alla Cabala.
#### La Cabala di Kerr

## Baatar

Baatar si trova ai margini settentrionali di [Lerei](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.lafidefp8m9x), dove i venti delle terre gelide incontrano le savane. Con un'estetica mongola-africana, i baatariani sono un popolo fiero, conosciuto per le loro vaste mandrie e i ventagli cerimoniali che simboleggiano il vento, la loro guida sacra. Vivono in tende decorate e spostano intere comunità per seguire i ritmi naturali del pianeta. Le tribù di Baatar sono unite da un codice d’onore che promuove la libertà e la lealtà, ma i conflitti tra clan rivali sono frequenti, soprattutto per l’accesso alle terre fertili di [Lerei](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.lafidefp8m9x).
## Samarkhoy

Estesa tra le foreste aride e le pianure montuose a nord di Lerei, Samarkhoy è una nazione in cui l'equilibrio tra giorno e notte domina ogni aspetto della cultura. Gli abitanti di Samarkhoy, noti per il loro artigianato di metalli rari e pietre preziose, sono maestri nella fusione di tradizioni antiche e innovazioni pratiche. Governata dalla [Regina Madre Zila’ach](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.z7yf5txfwif2), il cui regno è sorretto da un culto matriarcale, Samarkhoy venera le stelle e le loro danze celesti.  I villaggi sono spesso fortificati, non solo contro i predoni di [Kerr](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.ejeuytrw6wzr), ma anche contro le creature che emergono dalle terre gelide di [Eubdesh](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.bfh3j5b4fdvc).
#### Zila’ach, la Regina Madre

## Ashran

Situata lungo le fertili coste di [Lerei](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.lafidefp8m9x), Ashran è una nazione di marinai e agricoltori, modellata dalle brezze tiepide del Mare Interno e dalla perpetua luce dell’alba. Le sue città sono costruite su colline terrazzate, dove campi di riso e zafferano si alternano a templi di alabastro dedicati a divinità solari. Governata dal [Consiglio delle Grandi Voci](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nbV_9PrBD_mVn0p-k1_KOixiVuTaR453-2onC9Xa9jw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.e95g76xitxjw), un insieme di anziani scelti per saggezza e rettitudine, Ashran si distingue per la sua cultura spirituale e pacifica. Tuttavia, sotto la sua apparente tranquillità si cela una forza determinata, con abili guerrieri protettori delle sacre riserve d’acqua e delle foreste che lambiscono il deserto.
#### Il Consiglio delle Grandi Voci

## Gli altri

Oltre alle quattro nazioni, ci sono numerose tribù e popoli che abitano le regioni meno ospitali del pianeta. Briganti, nomadi, associazioni mercantili, da sole non hanno nessuna influenza ma tutte insieme possono sconvolgere gli equilibri politici.

bodies.name: Xan
bodies.descr:
Terra degli eretici.

### The Endless Siege

Xan is a planet caught in a never-ending state of conflict. Its surface is adorned with vibrant, yet perilous, flora that thrives in its lush environment. The dense vegetation is not only visually striking but also highly aggressive, creating a formidable natural defense that complements the planet's defensive architecture.

### The Giff and the Heretics

Xan is inhabited by two primary groups: the Giff and the Heretics. The Giff, a race of formidable and heavily armed creatures known for their military prowess and their formidable presence, are the primary defenders of Xan. They have constructed a network of fortified strongholds across the planet, each one a bastion against external threats. These fortresses are strategically placed to ensure comprehensive coverage and protection for the planet’s rich and vibrant ecosystems.

The Heretics, in contrast, are a faction with a more enigmatic and elusive nature. Their motives and goals often clash with the Giff, leading to internal strife and power struggles. Despite this, both groups share a common goal of preserving Xan's unique and thriving environment, albeit through different means and methods.

### The Inner Sun

One of Xan’s most distinctive features is its hollow interior, which houses an artificial sun created by the Giff. This mini sun is a marvel of engineering and magic, providing essential light and warmth to the planet's surface. It also plays a crucial role in sustaining the artificial ecosystems that simulate a full range of life forms.

This miniature sun is not merely a source of light but a vital component of Xan’s life-support system. It powers the creation of simulated food sources that sustain both the Giff and the Heretics. The intricate network of life-support systems and energy generation ensures that despite the constant conflict, life on Xan continues to thrive in a delicate balance.

### The Struggle for Survival

The planet’s inhabitants live in a constant state of vigilance and readiness. The overpopulation and the incessant threat of attack have led to a culture deeply ingrained with the need for defense and survival. Fortresses and defensive structures are not just military outposts but also vital parts of the planet’s infrastructure, supporting its dense and aggressive flora while safeguarding its inhabitants.

Xan’s beauty and richness come at the cost of perpetual vigilance and sacrifice. The blood of those who defend the planet is a testament to the high stakes of protecting such a valuable and vibrant world. Despite the constant siege, Xan’s fortifications and the tireless efforts of its defenders ensure that it remains unconquerable, a beacon of resilience amidst endless adversity.

bodies.name: Brion 7
bodies.descr:
Un pianeta schermato che protegge (o intrappola) qualcosa mai visto.

A blue, inscrutable shield covers this world, making it impossible to descend on the planet. Nevertheless, one can see through this shield to see green forests and oceans

# Description

### Arcane Shield
There is a shield covering the planet. It is impossible to teleport through it, it is immune to all damage, and cannot be dispelled. 

### Deathwalker (Spawn of Kyruss)
There is an impossibly destructive disease hidden in this world. Once a prosperous civilization of Elves, it is now a dead city, where even a small contact with a parasite might bring doom to all of the solar system.
